subtitle: How Saka Wanderers Forged a Western Indian Realm

panels.shot: epic wide shot of a rocky Western Indian coastline with a satrap-king in Indo-Scythian dress holding a coin and a rock-cut cave in the background
panels.action: Chashtana of the Western Kshatrapas stands on a wind-swept cliff above the western sea, one hand raised holding a gleaming silver coin, behind him loom rock-cut caves and an inscribed stone slab hinting at forgotten records.

dialogue.text: In a land without their own chronicles, Saka chiefs like Bhumaka, Nahapana and Chashtana left their story in silver, stone and caves, turning a foreign shore into their new Indian home.

i18n.hi: अपनी खुद की इतिहास‑पुस्तकों के बिना, भूमक, नहपान, चष्ठान जैसे शक सरदारों ने चाँदी, पत्थर और गुफाओं में अपना किस्सा छोड़ा, पराये तट को अपना नया भारतीय घर बना दिया।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from a single ancient coin to a table strewn with many coins and inscription rubbings
panels.action: A scholar’s wooden table centuries later lies under lamplight, scattered with Western Kshatrapa coins, inked impressions of Brahmi inscriptions and a map of western India marked with coastal and inland routes.

dialogue.text: No bard sang the full tale of the Western Kshatrapas. Instead, numismatists and epigraphers piece their lives from coins, cave gifts and wind-worn inscriptions across Gujarat, Saurashtra and Malwa.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी क्षत्रपों की पूरी गाथा कोई गायक नहीं गा पाया। सिक्कों, गुफा‑दानों और हवा से घिसी शिलालेखों से ही गुजरात, सौराष्ट्र और मालवा में उनके जीवन जोड़े जाते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a caravan approaching the western coast from the northwest, low angle to emphasize journey
panels.action: A long Saka caravan of horsemen and wagons winds down from dry northwestern plains toward a greener western Indian coast, Chashtana-like Saka nobles in tall caps watching the sea with wary curiosity.

dialogue.text: These Sakas, known in Greek notices as Scythians, came from the northwest steppes. By the first and second centuries, some had ridden far, to the salt breezes and busy ports of India’s western shore.

i18n.hi: यूनानी लेखों में स्किथियन कहे गए ये शक उत्तर‑पश्चिमी स्तेपी से आए। पहली‑दूसरी सदी तक कुछ घुड़सवार नमकीन समुंदर और चहल‑पहल वाले पश्चिमी भारतीय बंदरों तक पहुँच गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of an early satrap-king seated in audience with Indian merchants, balanced composition
panels.action: An Indo-Scythian satrap-king in mixed Saka and Indian dress sits on a low throne in a coastal hall, listening as Gujarati merchants in dhotis gesture toward routes on a palm-leaf map.

dialogue.text: Greek geographers later spoke of satraps along this coast. These were Saka chiefs who took Iranian titles like kshatrapa, yet dealt in Prakrit speech and Indian weights, ruling routes that fed Rome and the Deccan.

i18n.hi: यूनानी भूगोलकार बाद में इस तट के सतрапों का ज़िक्र करते हैं। ये शक सरदार ईरानी उपाधि ‘क्षत्रप’ धारण कर, प्राकृत बोलते, भारतीय तोल‑मोल अपनाते, और रोम व दक्खिन को जोड़ने वाले मार्गों पर राज करते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a freshly struck silver coin between tongs, fire glowing in the background
panels.action: A silversmith’s hand holds tongs gripping a freshly struck Western Kshatrapa coin, its Greek letters on one side and crisp Brahmi legend on the other catching the furnace light.

dialogue.text: From the Kshaharata line, Bhumaka’s coins speak first. They carry legends in Greek letters and in Brahmi, a Saka chief announcing himself in both the world he came from and the land he now ruled.

i18n.hi: क्षहरात वंश से भूमक के सिक्के पहले बोल उठते हैं। उन पर यूनानी अक्षर भी हैं और ब्राह्मी भी – एक शक मुखिया, पुरानी दुनिया और अपनी नई भारतीय धरती दोनों में अपना नाम उकेरता है।

panels.shot: top-down shot of several Bhumaka coins spread out, showing different symbols
panels.action: Several Bhumaka coins lie fanned on a rough cloth, some bearing a thunderbolt-like symbol, others a Buddhist chaitya, hinting at a variety of sacred and royal signs.

dialogue.text: Rapson read in those coins the name Bhūmaka, Kshaharata kshatrapa. Their symbols, thunderbolt and chaitya, hint at a court negotiating Vedic gods, Buddhist donors and older clan totems all at once.

i18n.hi: रैप्सन ने उन सिक्कों पर नाम पढ़ा – ‘भूमक क्षहरात क्षत्रप’। वज्र और चैत्य जैसे चिह्न बताते हैं कि दरबार एक साथ वैदिक देवों, बौद्ध दानियों और पुराने कुलचिह्नों से समझौता कर रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nahapana on a throne with officials around, coins laid before him, low angle
panels.action: A stern Indo-Scythian ruler, representing Nahapana, sits in a well-appointed hall, his council of Iranian-clad guards and Indian scribes around him, trays of fresh silver coins stacked at his feet.

dialogue.text: After Bhūmaka, coins proclaim a more powerful name: Nahapana of the Kshaharatas. His silver spread far, found today from Saurashtra to the Deccan, but no single sure year can be tied to his rule.

i18n.hi: भूमक के बाद सिक्के एक और भी प्रबल नाम का ढोल पीटते हैं – क्षहरात नहपान। उसका चाँदी‑जाल इतना फैला कि सौराष्ट्र से दक्खिन तक सिक्के मिलते हैं, पर उसकी हुकूमत से जुड़ी पक्की तारीख नहीं मिलती।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling western port city with ships and warehouses, atmospheric haze
panels.action: A bustling port city lines the western coast, with wooden jetties, Roman-style ships at anchor, warehouse rows and Nahapana’s officials overseeing bales of cotton and jars of spices.

dialogue.text: Nahapana’s realm joined Saurashtra, Gujarat and the western Deccan ports. His administration, glimpsed through coin hoards and later cave records, sat astride trade that tied inland Satavahanas to the Indian Ocean.

i18n.hi: नहपान का इलाका सौराष्ट्र, गुजरात और पश्चिमी दक्खिन के बंदरगाहों को जोड़ता था। सिक्कों के खज़ानों और बाद की गुफा‑लेखों में दिखता है कि उसकी हुकूमत सतवाहनों और हिंद महासागर के बीच की व्यापार‑कड़ी पर बैठी थी।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a rock-cut cave under construction, workers chiseling, donor figures watching
panels.action: Inside a half-carved rock-cut cave in the western ghats, artisans hammer at pillars while robed donors and a satrap official inspect the emerging chaitya hall, the cliff opening onto forested valleys.

dialogue.text: Cave inscriptions near Nashik and elsewhere record gifts in Nahapana’s time, naming his family and feudatories. They show Saka satraps patronising rock-cut shrines, weaving their authority into local sacred landscapes.

i18n.hi: नाशिक व आसपास की गुफा‑लिपियों में नहपान के ज़माने के दान दर्ज हैं, जिनमें उसके कुल और सामंतों के नाम हैं। वे दिखाती हैं कि शक क्षत्रप शैल‑मंदिरों को दान देकर अपनी सत्ता को स्थानीय तीर्थ‑भूमि में बुन रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on an inscription being chiseled in Brahmi on a cave wall, with Nahapana’s name mid-line
panels.action: A mason carefully chisels Brahmi characters into a cave wall, Nahapana’s name just taking shape as a scribe beside him reads from a palm-leaf, the letters crisp against the stone.

dialogue.text: Here the Saka chief’s Iranian title, kshatrapa, sits in a Prakrit sentence written in Brahmi. The language of Ashoka now carries foreign rulers’ names, a sign of how deeply they had stepped into India’s script and speech.

i18n.hi: यहाँ शक सरदार की ईरानी उपाधि ‘क्षत्रप’ ब्राह्मी में लिखे प्राकृत वाक्य के बीच बैठी है। अशोक की भाषा अब विदेशी शासकों के नाम ढोती है – ये चिन्ह है कि वे भारत की लिपि और बोली में कितना गहरे उतर गए थे।

panels.shot: transition shot dissolving from Nahapana’s coins to a new coin type bearing Chashtana’s name
panels.action: The frame shows Nahapana’s coin stack fading into a different set of coins bearing Chashtana’s name, as if history itself is turning a page through gleaming metal discs.

dialogue.text: But coins also tell of change. The Kshaharata line fades; a new clan, the Kardamakas, stamp their mark. With Chashtana, another Saka house rises as western kshatrapas in the Saka era.

i18n.hi: पर सिक्के बदलाव की कहानी भी कहते हैं। क्षहरात वंश धुंधला पड़ता है; नया कुल, कार्दमक, अपनी मुहर लगाता है। चष्ठान के साथ एक और शक घराना शक युग के पश्चिमी क्षत्रपों के रूप में उठ खड़ा होता है।

panels.shot: wide rural shot of Andhau region with a stone pillar bearing inscription, Chashtana standing nearby
panels.action: In the dry landscape of Andhau in Kutch, Chashtana stands beside a newly raised inscribed stone pillar, Kardamaka retainers behind him, as villagers look on cautiously from a distance.

dialogue.text: At Andhau and Khavada in Kutch, Chashtana’s family left inscriptions. Sircar read in them the early Kardamaka genealogy and dates counted in a new Saka era that would anchor many later Indian records.

i18n.hi: कच्छ के अँधाउ और खवड़ा में चष्ठान के कुल ने शिलालेख छोड़े। सिरकार ने उनमें शुरुआती कार्दमक वंशावली और नए शक युग की तिथियाँ पढ़ीं, जो बाद के कई भारतीय लेखों के लिए आधार बनीं।

panels.shot: close-up of the Andhau inscription face, showing the Saka era date and Chashtana’s titles
panels.action: The camera lingers on the face of the Andhau stone, its Brahmi letters crisp, the Saka year numerals and Chashtana’s titles clearly visible under a slant of afternoon light.

dialogue.text: Salomon notes how these early Saka-era records are few and debated. Yet they anchor Chashtana in time, a Saka satrap using Indian numerals and Prakrit words to fix his family in the memory of the land.

i18n.hi: सालोमन बताता है कि ये शुरुआती शक‑युग शिलालेख कम हैं और विवादित भी, फिर भी वे चष्ठान को समय में गाड़ देते हैं – एक शक क्षत्रप, जो भारतीय अंकों और प्राकृत शब्दों से अपने कुल को इस धरती की याद में पक्का करता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chashtana in council with Brahmin scribes and local chiefs, balanced composition
panels.action: Chashtana sits in council with Brahmin scribes holding styluses, and local Indian chiefs with folded hands; a scroll between them shows both Saka clan names and local place names carefully written.

dialogue.text: Under Chashtana, Kardamaka satraps ruled through local elites and scribes. Their inscriptions mix Saka family names with Gujarat and Saurashtra places, bridging steppe ancestry and western Indian soil.

i18n.hi: चष्ठान के अधीन कार्दमक क्षत्रपों ने स्थानीय सर्दारों और लेखकों के ज़रिए राज चलाया। उनके लेखों में शक कुलनाम, गुजरात‑सौराष्ट्र की जगहों के साथ मिलकर, स्तेपी की वंश‑जड़ों को पश्चिमी भारतीय मिट्टी से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a rock-cut cave façade with multiple donor figures carved, sea visible beyond
panels.action: A completed rock-cut cave façade stands high above the western plains, carved donor figures lining its veranda while the distant sea shimmers, suggesting a world of traders and rulers passing by below.

dialogue.text: Cave records from this age show donors with Saka, Indian and guild names side by side. Western Kshatrapas were not alone here; they ruled among merchants, monks and craftsmen who also etched themselves into stone.

i18n.hi: इस दौर की गुफा‑लिपियों में शक, भारतीय और विभिन्न श्रेणी‑संगठनों के दानदाताओं के नाम साथ‑साथ हैं। पश्चिमी क्षत्रप अकेले नहीं थे; वे व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं और कारीगरों के बीच राज कर रहे थे, जो खुद को भी पत्थर पर उकेर रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a later inscription mentioning Rudradaman, with Chashtana named as ancestor, shallow depth of field
panels.action: A later, finely carved inscription panel names Rudradaman in bold letters, while Chashtana’s name appears earlier in the line, the older generation engraved with equal care.

dialogue.text: Later, Rudradaman would boast of Chashtana as ancestor. The Kardamaka house, still Saka by origin, now used polished Sanskrit in its proclamations, showing how deeply the satraps had learned the languages of India.

i18n.hi: बाद में रुद्रदामन चष्ठान को अपना पूर्वज कहकर गर्व करेगा। कार्दमक घराना, मूल से शक होकर भी, अब चमकदार संस्कृत में शिलालेख लिखवाता है – दिखाते हुए कि क्षत्रप भारत की भाषाएँ कितनी गहराई से सीख चुके थे।

panels.shot: montage shot: coins, cave interiors, coastal ports and inscriptions all layered semi-transparently
panels.action: The frame layers images of Western Kshatrapa coins, rock-cut cave interiors, bustling coastal ports and inscribed stones, creating a tapestry of the material traces left by these Saka satraps.

dialogue.text: From Bhumaka’s first coins to Nahapana’s trade routes and Chashtana’s Saka-era pillars, we see foreigners gradually rooted: their marks in silver, in rock, in scripts woven into Indian public life.

i18n.hi: भूमक के पहले सिक्कों से लेकर नहपान के व्यापार‑मार्गों और चष्ठान के शक‑युग के स्तंभों तक, हम देखते हैं कि परदेसी धीरे‑धीरे जड़ें जमाते हैं – उनकी छाप चाँदी में, चट्टान में, और भारतीय जन‑जीवन की लिपियों में।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Chashtana standing at a cliff edge at dusk, looking over his lands, contemplative
panels.action: At dusk, Chashtana stands once more on a cliff above the western plain, his Saka cap silhouetted, the lights of villages and caravan fires pricking the darkening land below.

dialogue.speaker: bhumaka_nahapana_and_chashtana
dialogue.text: A land is not taken by hooves alone; it is held by service.

i18n.hi: धरा केवल घोड़ों की टाप से नहीं, सेवा से थामी जाती है।

panels.shot: pull-back to a vast view of western India with trade routes glowing faintly like lines across the land
panels.action: The camera pulls back to reveal a vast map-like view of western India, caravan and sea routes glowing faintly across Gujarat, Saurashtra and Malwa, with ghostly images of Bhumaka, Nahapana and Chashtana hovering above.

dialogue.text: Their chronicles are lost, yet their coins and inscriptions endure, reminding us that newcomers can become builders when they learn a land’s language, share its shrines and stake their memory in its stone.

i18n.hi: उनकी इतिहास‑पुस्तकें खो गईं, पर सिक्के और शिलालेख आज भी ज़िंदा हैं, याद दिलाते हुए कि जब नये आने वाले किसी भूमि की भाषा सीखें, उसके तीर्थ बाँटें और अपना स्मारक वहीं गाड़ें, तो वे भी उसके निर्माता बन जाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Saka Satraps Make India Home
title_i18n.hi: शक क्षत्रपों ने भारत को घर बनाया

subtitle_i18n.en: How Saka Wanderers Forged a Western Indian Realm
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे भटकते शक बने पश्चिमी भारत के शासक
